title: Sean Stone’s 10 Things to Learn: Ancient Wisdom for the Modern Soul
description:
10 Things to Learn: Ancient Wisdom for the Modern Soul explores what it means to remain fully human in an age increasingly defined by technology, optimization, and artificial intelligence. While modern civilization has expanded humanity’s power and capability, it has done little to eliminate suffering, grief, fear, or the search for meaning. This book argues that life’s deepest questions cannot be answered through efficiency or control. Instead, genuine growth emerges through a series of essential initiations—moments of collapse, surrender, loss, rest, and devotion that shape the soul. Blending mythology, philosophy, memoir, and poetic reflection, it offers a timeless framework for navigating the emotional and spiritual disorientation of modern life.

Structured around ten symbolic “gates,” the book reframes life as a cyclical journey of awakening rather than a linear pursuit of success. These gates—Falling, Surrendering, Crying, Caring, Hating, Creating, Sharing, Loving, Breathing, and Laughing—each represent a threshold of psychological and spiritual transformation. Drawing from Greek mythology, Biblical narratives, Eastern philosophy, and archetypal storytelling, the book presents a unified map of human development. Its voice combines lyrical prose with intellectual rigor, placing it at the intersection of Joseph Campbell’s mythological insight, Alan Watts’s spiritual inquiry, and the literary introspection of Hermann Hesse.

At a time of accelerating technological change, rising anxiety, and the erosion of traditional sources of meaning, 10 Things to Learn offers something increasingly rare: not just insight, but initiation. It speaks to readers seeking coherence in a fragmented world and restores a sense of purpose through the defining ordeals of the human experience.

Joe Maxwell is a fourth-generation Missouri farmer, former Missouri Lieutenant Governor, and nationally recognized advocate for fair and competitive markets. Through Redbird, Rev. Cerveny has ministered to professional athletes, journalists, politicians, pastors, and priests. He and his wife of 21 years, Charla, live in Jacksonville, Florida, with their three children (Emmy, Wiley, and Scout) and their Cavalier King Charles Spaniel, Lolly. title: On Implossibility (No, Spell-Check Didn’t Fail Me)
description:
Jorge Luis Borges’s story “The Library of Babel” describes an astronomically large (if not infinite) library. The library is an innumerable collection of hexagonal rooms, each containing floor-to-ceiling bookshelves filled with books.
